Subject: Transient GPU crediting + phased burst cadence for Orion Labs Dedicated

Hi Sam / Elena —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together a short set of options for how we can structure "transient burst" capacity on your Dedicated pool so you have predictable headroom during peak training windows without overcommitting reserved slabs. Key constraints we discussed: 1) short high-concurrency episodes (30–90m), 2) steady inference baseline during business hours, 3) procurement prefers spend predictability.

Can you confirm the three weekly windows where you see the 2–3x token throughput spikes (days/times in your timezone) and the approximate peak concurrent jobs during those windows? If you can attach a 7‑day sample (CSV) of request volumes, that will help me size the burst slab and the temporary crediting policy.

I'll draft two concrete policies:
- Phased burst (preferred): pre-authorized ephemeral credits cumulative to a monthly cap. Credits auto-consume and fall back to a cheaper model variant when exhausted.
- On-demand burst: live autoscale that pulls from shared cloud capacity with a higher per-minute premium and eviction rules.

I want to highlight SLO behavior: we can guarantee baseline latency for reserved capacity. For burst episodes we provide a tiered SLA during pre-warmed windows and a best-effort fallback outside them.

Attached: a short checklist of data points we need.

Next step: if you send the sample CSV + preferred days/times, we'll produce a sizing recommendation and an estimated monthly burn (credits + minutes).

Thanks,

Sam / Procurement team —

Appreciate the quick data. Based on the sample, here is a concise proposal (high level) for two options. I'll keep cost math conservative to give Procurement room to negotiate.

Option A — Phased Credits (recommended):
- Mechanism: Purchase a monthly pool of transient credits that convert 1:1 to GPU-minute equivalents on the Dedicated cluster during pre-authorized windows. Credits expire monthly.
- Pre-warm windows: we mark Tue 09:00–11:00 and Thu 14:30–16:45 (PST) as pre-warm; Saturday peak treated as overnight burst with lower pre-warm SLA.
- Headroom sizing: reserve an additional 120 GPU-minutes per peak episode (equivalent to ~4 extra A100s for 45–75 minutes) which covers the observed 2–3x concurrency spikes with ~15% buffer. Monthly estimate: ~3,200 transient GPU-minutes => estimated credits spend $X (see attached PDF for line items).
- Failover: when credits are exhausted, traffic is routed to pinned cheaper model variants or queued with progressive shedding.
- Pros: Predictable monthly spend, simple reconciliation, better latency during pre-warm windows.

Option B — On-demand Burst (pay-as-you-use):
- Mechanism: Live autoscale pulls from cloud-backed ephemeral nodes; billed per-minute at a premium rate.
- No monthly commitment but higher unit cost. Eviction rules apply under extreme cluster contention (we provide eviction ordering + customer-owned notification hooks).
- Pros: Lower upfront commitment; Cons: less predictable and possible transient elevated latencies.

Security & compliance: we will expose audit logs for burst events (timestamped scaling decisions, model variant fallbacks) to your SIEM via a delivered log sink. We'll include an SLA appendix describing the pre-warm guarantees and a table of accepted failure modes.

Attached: orion-burst-proposal-v1.pdf (contains the cost table, eviction policies, and a suggested contract clause for transient credits).

Action items:
- Procurement: confirm which option you want priced into the MSA (credits vs on-demand).
- Engineering (Elena): can you confirm whether you need memory-capped pods for batch scoring jobs so we size the per-GPU memory headroom?

Happy to hop on a 30m call to walk through numbers.

— Vivek
